title: Siemens SM0901 CRT no display / black screen: technical specs
body_devto:
## Technical Details

When replacing a Siemens SM0901 CRT, check three things: (1) connector type — DB-25 (25-pin D-Sub), (2) power supply — AC 110V, (3) control system — SINUMERIK 810, SINUMERIK 820, SINUMERIK 840D. All three are covered by the standard LCD upgrade. Price: $299.

A blank CRT often means the flyback transformer (high-voltage section) has failed completely. This component steps up power to 20-30kV — when it goes, there's no image at all.

## Cost Comparison: Repair vs Replace

| Option | Cost | Lifespan |
|--------|------|----------|
| CRT repair (rebuilt HV section) | $299–598 each | 3-12 months |
| CRT repair (donor tube swap) | $399–599 | 6-18 months |
| Used CRT on eBay | $598–897 | Unknown (already aged) |
| LCD replacement module | $299 (one-time) | 5-7 years continuous |

Most shops break even on LCD cost within 12 months by eliminating just one CRT failure.

⚠️ Siemens uses AC 110V — do NOT use a DC-only LCD module or it will be destroyed on power-up.

## Installation

1. Power off CNC machine and verify power is off with multimeter
2. Remove 4 mounting bolts from the CRT bezel
3. Disconnect the DB-25 cable
4. Connect same cable to the replacement LCD module
5. Mount LCD using original screw holes (same pattern)
6. Power on — no CNC parameter changes required

Total time: ~15 minutes. The LCD draws AC 110V, matching the original CRT power supply.

Full guide: https://cncdisplay.com/brands/Siemens.html

## Summary

Every Siemens 6FC3988-7FA20 CRT will eventually fail. Plan the upgrade now instead of scrambling during a production emergency. Details: https://cncdisplay.com/brands/Siemens.html
